sentences.text:
The Honourable Sri Justice Sambasiva Rao Naidu
 Criminal Appeal No.791 Of 2012
Judgment:

This Criminal Appeal has been filed, under Section 374(2) of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 (for brevity 'Cr.P.C') by accused No.1 in S.C.No.136 of 2011 on the file of the Additional District Judge-cum-Family Judge, Nalgonda (for short 'trial Court'), challenging the Judgment dated 01.08.2012 whereunder the trial Court having found accused Nos.1 to 4 not guilty for the offences under Sections 306 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short 'IPC') and also having found accused Nos.2 to 4 not guilty for the offence under Section 498A of IPC while found accused No.1 guilty for the offence under Section 498A of IPC and convicted him under Section 235(2) of Cr.P.C. and sentenced him to undergo rigorous imprisonment for a period of three (03) years and to pay a fine of Rs.2,000/- with default sentence, with a prayer to set aside the above referred sentence on the following grounds:
The Judgment of the trial Court is contrary to law and weight of evidence.
The trial Court committed an error in passing conviction only on the basis of mere presumptions and assumptions without considering the discrepancies in the evidence of PWs.1 to 3.
The trial Court ought to have considered that PWs.4 to 7, who were the material witnesses to the case, did not support the prosecution and no dowry harassment was attributed to the appellant.
He has claimed that the trial Court passed a conviction without there being any evidence with regard to the dowry demand or acceptance of the dowry by the appellant.

He has claimed that the trial Court failed to observe that there is no such demand which can attract the provisions of Section 498A of IPC, thereby, instead of acquittal, passed an incorrect sentence as such he sought for setting aside the impugned Judgment.

2. Before adverting to the grounds raised by the appellant/accused No.1 in the present appeal and appreciating the arguments of learned counsel for the appellant/accused No.1 as well as learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for the respondent- State, it is just and necessary to examine what is the case that was filed against the appellant herein.

3. According to the charge sheet filed against the appellant and his family members, it was briefly stated that one Smt.Dandu Janakamma, who is the de facto complainant, lodged a complaint before the police with the specific allegations that about 1 years prior to her complaint, she performed the marriage of her daughter, namely, Swarnalatha (hereinafter referred to as 'the deceased') with the appellant herein and at the time of marriage, she presented 11 tulas of gold, 26 tulas of silver,
cash of Rs.61,000/- and also house hold articles to the appellant herein.

After marriage, the deceased joined the appellant at his house but the appellant including the other accused Nos.2 to 4 subjected the deceased to harassment both physically and mentally on the ground that she is not Daku Venkatesham vs The State Of A.P. on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169663170/
1 attending agricultural works and she could not conceive even 1 years of the marriage and that several panchayats were held in the village but there was no change in the attitude of the accused.

sentences.text: She also informed the police that on 15.07.2010 she received a phone call from the deceased stating that she was proceeding to the hospital to Bommalaramaram and asked her to join her at the hospital and that after the medical examination, there was dispute/galata arose between the appellant and PW.1, with regard to the payment of Doctor consultation fee as the appellant informed PW.1 that they have paid Rs.600/- towards Doctor fee and demanded her to pay half of the said amount.

PW.1 has also informed the police that on the next day i.e., on 16.07.2010 at about 02.00 P.M. she received a call from her younger brother and she was informed about the suicide committed by the deceased.
Therefore, she suspected the involvement of the accused and requested the police to take appropriate action.

4. Basing on the complaint lodged by PW.1, police have registered a case in Crime No.30 of 2010,
issued FIR and after completion of the investigation laid the charge sheet against the accused for the offences under Sections 498A and 306 of IPC.
The said charge sheet was initially registered as PRC and later it was committed to the Sessions Court.
The trial Court having framed the charges under Sections 498A and 306 of IPC, proceeded with the trial.

5. According to the averments made in the charge sheet, it was specifically contended that accused Nos.1 to 4 being husband and in-laws of the deceased on the ground that she could not conceive during the marital tie and failed to attend agricultural works along with them, they subjected her to cruelty and abetted her to suicidal death.

However, after the conclusion of the full-fledged trial, the trial Court came to the conclusion that the prosecution was not able to prove the guilt of the accused for the offence under Section 306 of IPC holding that there was no such abetment or instigation by the accused which resulted to commission of suicide by the deceased.

However, the trial Court recorded that the prosecution failed to bring home the guilt of accused Nos.2 to 4 for the offences under Section 498A of IPC and accordingly, acquitted all the accused for the offence under Section 306 of IPC as well as accused Nos.2 to 4 for the offence under Section 498A of IPC.

However, the trial Court came to the conclusion that the evidence of all the witnesses, more particularly, the mother and the other relatives of the deceased clearly shows that the appellant/accused No.1 being husband of the deceased subjected her to cruelty, thereby, she committed suicide and thereby, he is liable for punishment under Section 498A of IPC.

6. Now, the points that would emerge for determination in this appeal are:
1) Whether the trial Court failed to appreciate the evidence in appropriate way and came to the incorrect conclusion about the guilt of the appellant/accused No.1?
2) Whether the accused is entitled for the acquittal as prayed for?
7.

As already stated that the appellant herein was charged under Sections 306 and 498A of IPC,
there is a clear finding by which the trial Court found that the charge under Section 306 of IPC was not been proved against the appellant herein.
To prove its case, the prosecution has examined PWs.1 to 16 and marked Exs.P.1 to P.12 and M.O.1.
The appellant herein did not examine any witness but Daku Venkatesham vs The State Of A.P. on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169663170/

sentences.text: 2 marked contradictions elicited from PW.9 from the statements made before the police under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. and marked as Exs.D.1 and D.2.
It seems the material witnesses i.e., PWs.4, 5, 6 and 7 turned hostile and did not support the prosecution.

As per the testimony of the witnesses, PW.1-De facto complainant was examined to prove the marriage of the deceased with the appellant/accused No.1 and also to prove the alleged harassment or cruelty done by the appellant/accused No.1 to the deceased.
PW.2, who is the grandfather of the deceased, was only the circumstantial witness to prove the payment of dowry and subsequent harassment made by the accused.
PW.3, who is the brother of PW.1, was examined to prove the alleged harassment made by the accused.
PWs.4 to 7 turned hostile and they did not support the case of the prosecution.

8. According to the evidence of PW.8, he acted as an elder for an alleged panchayat raised by PW.1 with a specific claim that the accused were harassing her daughter on the ground that she could not conceive and not attending the agricultural works.
PW.8 is not a material witness to prove the dowry harassment or cruelty made by the accused.

PW.9 is a Registered Medical Practitioner and according to his evidence, one day prior to the suicide/death of the deceased, she was taken to his hospital for medical examination with regard to the stomach pain and she could not conceive.
PW.9 was examined to prove that there was a quarrel held between PW.1 and the appellant/accused No.1 in connection with the payment of medical charges.
The other witnesses are only circumstantial witnesses, who may not depose anything about the dowry harassment or cruelty said to have been done by the accused.

9. Per contra, the defence of the accused is very specific, according to his case before the trial Court and as per the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant, he contended that there was no such cruelty or dowry harassment as alleged and that the accused belongs to poor family and they used to eke out their livelihood by attending the agricultural works and that there was no wrong in asking the deceased to attend the agriculture works.

However, they have also contended that the deceased, who was suffering from severe stomach pain and who could not tolerate the pain,
committed suicide after the medical examination done by PW.9 and also contended that they never subjected her to cruelty or dowry harassment.

10. In order to prove the offence under Section 498A of IPC, there must be some positive evidence on behalf of the prosecution to believe that the accused subjected the deceased to cruelty within the meaning of Section 498A of IPC and due to which the deceased attempted to end her life.

In the instant case on hand, even though omnibus allegations were made by PW.1 and her family members that there was dowry demand, the oral evidence of all the witnesses indicates that both the families belong to below poverty line where there is a custom that female persons also used to attend agricultural works.

Further, PW.1 herself deposed before the trial Court that there were quarrels at the house of the accused on the ground that the deceased could not conceive even after lapse of 1 years of marital tie.

If the appellant/accused No.1 and his family members expressed any anguish or dissatisfaction on the ground that the deceased could not give birth to the child even after more than one year of marital tie, it cannot be said that it is with an intention to drive the deceased to commit suicide.

sentences.text: It is nothing but natural, in villages where the people are not much educated and they are particular about the child birth and that they might have asked the deceased to give birth to a child and for that purpose they have taken the deceased to PW.9 for medical examination.

Therefore, the allegation of PW.1 and her family members that accused subjected the deceased to harassment and instigated her to commit suicide to bring additional dowry from the family cannot be accepted, more particularly, in the absence of the evidence of any independent witnesses.

The trial Court even though came to the conclusion that there is no evidence to believe that the accused abetted the suicidal death of the deceased, came to an incorrect conclusion that accused No.1 is liable for the punishment under Section 498A of IPC.
The only allegation that is leveled against the appellant herein is he used to make comments on the deceased as if she did not conceive.

The trial Court recorded a finding that the appellant/accused No.1 married the deceased and lead marital life only for small period and later, he harassed her as she did not conceive, thereby, it means to mental cruelty.

In fact, the evidence of PWs.1 to 3 and 9 depicts that the deceased did not conceive even after 1 years of marital tie and also as the deceased complained severe stomach pain, they took the deceased to PW.9 for opinion.
12.

It transpires from the evidence of PW.1 that soon after the marriage, the appellant herein and his wife lived together while the other accused used to reside at Indira Nagar and thereupon, the appellant and the deceased shifted their residence to Malkajgiri locality, Secunderabad, to a rented house.

Therefore, the trial Court in spite of the fact that there is no sufficient evidence to show that accused No.1 was having mensria to harass his wife and subjected her to cruelty only on the ground of not begotten children is not an offence under Section 498A of IPC.
Except the evidence of interested witnesses, there was no other evidence offered by the prosecution to believe the alleged mental cruelty made by the appellant herein.

13. After meticulously scanning the entire material placed before this Court, having regard to the facts and circumstances and, be it viewed from any angle, this Court is of the considered opinion that the trial Court was wrong in came to the conclusion that the appellant/accused No.1 subjected his wife to cruelty or mental cruelty, therefore, the appellant/accused No.1 is entitled to benefit of doubt and the trial Court could not have convicted him for the offence under Section 498A of IPC
as such the appeal deserves to be allowed.
14. In view of the discussion made hereinbefore, this Criminal Appeal is allowed, setting aside the impugned Judgment dated 01.08.2012 passed in S.C.No.136 of 2011 by the trial Court.
As a consequence thereof, the appellant/accused No.1 is acquitted for the offence under Section 498A of IPC.
Pending miscellaneous application, if any, shall stand closed.

_ _ JUSTICE SAMBASIVA RAO NAIDU DATED 14.02.2024 YNK Daku Venkatesham vs The State Of A.P. on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169663170/
